report.summary: Chunk 6 of 8: wiki target resolution logic, KnowledgeLinks dataclass, and knowledge_links function. No critical issues.

handoff.purpose: Implements resolve_wiki_target, resolve_wiki_links, KnowledgeLinks dataclass, and knowledge_links function.

symbols.name: resolve_wiki_target
symbols.note: Resolves a single wikilink target to (rel or None, status). Appends default_ext only when raw name matches nothing.

symbols.name: resolve_wiki_links
symbols.note: Returns list of (DocLink, target or None, status) for every wikilink in document order. Handles deferred and self-links.

symbols.name: KnowledgeLinks
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding all relations asserted by one document, plus counts for unresolved/ambiguous/deferred/external.

symbols.name: KnowledgeLinks.to_dict
symbols.note: Converts KnowledgeLinks instance to a dict with lists for targets and counts.

symbols.name: knowledge_links
symbols.note: Combines standard links and wikilinks, resolved, with counts. Returns KnowledgeLinks.

claims.text: default_ext is appended ONLY as a second round, when the name as written matches nothing: [[Note]] finds Note.md, while ![[chart.png]] still finds the png rather than hunting for chart.png.md.
claims.why: In the code, forms = [raw]; if default_ext and not raw.lower().endswith(default_ext): forms.append(raw + default_ext). Then for form in forms: ... This ensures the default_ext is tried only after the raw form fails.

claims.text: [(link, target or None, status)] for every wikilink, in document order.
claims.why: The function returns out, which is built by iterating parse.wiki_links in order and appending (link, target, status).

claims.text: A document linking to itself is not an edge -- the rule internal_links already applies, restated here rather than left to the caller.
claims.where: resolve_wiki_links, comment inside if target == parse.document
claims.why: When target == parse.document, the code appends (link, None, WIKI_RESOLVED) and continues, effectively treating it as resolved but not an edge.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT folded into internal_links: that function is the contract index.py builds document_links from today, and doc->code is a different relation from doc->doc.
claims.why: The docstring references internal_links and index.py which are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Standard links AND wikilinks, resolved, with every refusal counted.
claims.why: The function calls internal_links (standard links) and resolve_wiki_links (wikilinks), and counts ambiguous, deferred, unresolved.

claims.text: doc_targets is a superset of internal_links' first return value: same standard-markdown edges, plus the wikilink ones.
claims.why: The function does call internal_links and uses its first return value (std_targets) as the initial set for doc_targets, but the internal_links function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: code_targets is kept apart on purpose (see KnowledgeLinks), and type_refs carries names this module never tried to resolve.
claims.why: The code maintains separate sets: code, types. For links with kind 'type', it adds to types and does not attempt resolution.

observations.what: The function resolve_wiki_target uses raw.lower().endswith(default_ext) to decide whether to append default_ext. This may cause issues if default_ext is empty (which is allowed) because raw.lower().endswith('') is always True, so the condition will be False and the extension won't be appended. However, the docstring says default_ext is appended only as a second round; the code's logic seems correct because if default_ext is empty, no second form is needed.
observations.where: resolve_wiki_target, line with 'if default_ext and not raw.lower().endswith(default_ext):'

observations.what: In resolve_wiki_links, when target == parse.document, the code appends (link, None, WIKI_RESOLVED). This departs from the function's general pattern of returning the target as the second element; here it returns None for self-links. The docstring says 'target or None', so this is consistent.

The variable 'types' in knowledge_links is only populated when status == WIKI_DEFERRED and link.kind == 'type'. However, the KnowledgeLinks dataclass has a field 'type_refs' that is documented as 'RESOLVED BY NOBODY'. This matches the code.
